name: Bizta
title: Eunuch in the service of King Ahasuerus
summary: Bizta was one of the seven eunuchs (court officials) who served King Ahasuerus (Xerxes I) of Persia. He is mentioned in the book of Esther in connection with the great banquet where the king sent his eunuchs to fetch Queen Vashti. Bizta plays a small, but named role in the events that led to Vashti's deposition and Esther's elevation to queen.

keyEvents.title: The King's Great Banquet
keyEvents.description: King Ahasuerus held a magnificent banquet that lasted 180 days to display the wealth and splendor of his kingdom, followed by a seven-day banquet for all in the citadel of Susa.

keyEvents.title: Sent to fetch Queen Vashti
keyEvents.description: On the seventh day of the feast, when the king was merry with wine, he commanded Bizta and the six other eunuchs to bring Queen Vashti before him wearing the royal crown, so that she might be shown to the people and the princes for her beauty.

keyEvents.title: Queen Vashti refuses to come
keyEvents.description: Queen Vashti refused to come at the king's command delivered by the eunuchs, which aroused great anger in the king.

keyEvents.title: The consequences of Vashti's refusal
keyEvents.description: Vashti's rejection led to counsel from the king's wise men and ultimately her removal as queen, paving the way for Esther.
